# Personalization as a sales lever for Lee’s Market
**For Michael Lee, Sales Team Lead**

## How personalization can grow retail sales
Relevant product suggestions and offers can help shoppers discover complementary or new products, add items to a basket, convert online visits, and return for repeat trips. McKinsey reports that personalized retail experiences are associated with stronger customer loyalty and gross sales. Its research also found that 71% of consumers expect personalized interactions and 76% get frustrated when they do not receive them. These findings support investing in relevance, but they do not establish a guaranteed sales lift for Lee’s. McKinsey’s finding that faster-growing companies derive 40% more revenue from personalization is a comparison between company groups, not a causal uplift estimate. ([Retail personalization](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/retail/our-insights/personalizing-the-customer-experience-driving-differentiation-in-retail); [consumer study](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/growth-marketing-and-sales/our-insights/the-value-of-getting-personalization-right-or-wrong-is-multiplying); [growth comparison](https://www.mckinsey.com/featured-insights/mckinsey-explainers/what-is-personalization))

## Lee’s starting point
An internal 2023 retail strategy document reports that 45% of online customers engaged with personalized recommendations and attributes a 25% increase in average order value to those recommendations. It does not provide a sample size, measurement window, baseline, or comparison group, so treat the 25% as a promising reported association to validate, not a proven incremental result. Separately, a Sales Strategy post says about 85% of transactions were linked to loyalty accounts by Q2 2024, up from the prior quarter. That gives Lee’s a useful data foundation; it is not evidence that personalization has already increased sales. (`Retail-Growth-Strategies-2023.docx`; `Mattermost Message - Enterprise Chat (User: samantha.kim, Team: Sales Team, Channel: Sales Strategy)`)

## Recommended actions
1. **Turn loyalty-linked purchases into relevant weekly offers.** Use purchase recency, frequency, and category affinity to recommend complementary products, encourage trial in adjacent categories, and win back lapsed shoppers. Track gross margin after discount cost so higher redemption does not mask unprofitable sales.
2. **Make online merchandising useful for a real meal or trip.** Test cuisine- and occasion-based recipe bundles that connect Lee’s fresh produce, meats and seafood, bakery or prepared foods, and pantry items. Add replenishment reminders based on a shopper’s own buying cadence. Use stated cuisine, language, and dietary preferences where customers choose to share them.
3. **Personalize around availability across web, delivery, and stores.** When an item is unavailable, suggest an in-stock alternative that fits the shopper’s chosen dietary or product preferences. Carry the order and preference context into customer-service handoffs so an agent can resolve a substitution or refund and update the customer’s choices.
4. **Improve transaction matching with an optional loyalty prompt.** Build on the reported 85% transaction linkage by making enrollment and account lookup easy at checkout and online; do not infer cuisine or dietary preferences from ethnicity. Be transparent about how profile data is used and let customers change their preferences. The Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada’s PIPEDA guidance provides a reference for responsible handling of personal information. ([PIPEDA guidance](https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/privacy-topics/privacy-laws-in-canada/the-personal-information-protection-and-electronic-documents-act-pipeda/))

## Pilot and scorecard
Run a 6–8 week pilot in a limited set of stores and online, with a randomized business-as-usual holdout and stable customer assignment across channels. Size the test using Lee’s baseline transaction volume and allow enough follow-up to observe a repeat purchase. Compare customers by their assigned group, not only by who opened an offer or redeemed a coupon.

Use **incremental gross margin per eligible loyalty customer** as the primary measure, net of discount and fulfillment costs. Track total sales, basket value, online conversion, promoted-category attachment, 30- and 60-day repeat purchase, redemption, substitution acceptance, and opt-outs or complaints as secondary measures. Check stockouts and unmatched transactions before scaling. A randomized holdout will show whether the internal AOV signal generalizes to Lee’s broader customer base and whether the lift is profitable.

Grocery research describes loyalty data, tailored incentives, and recommendations as parts of a connected shopping experience; vendor guidance also describes applying purchase history and category affinity to offers across app, web, and checkout. These sources support the tactics, not a forecast of Lee’s results. ([Coresight grocery report](https://coresight.com/research/five-strategies-for-success-in-us-grocery-retail-leveraging-first-party-data-to-offer-a-connected-shopping-experience/); [Birdzi grocery offers](https://birdzi.com/digital-coupons-vs-personalized-offers-roi/))

report_insights.claim: Retail personalization can support sales by making product discovery and offers more relevant, and McKinsey associates personalized experiences with higher customer loyalty and gross sales. Consumer expectations are high: 71% expect personalized interactions and 76% report frustration when they do not receive them.

McKinsey reports faster-growing companies derive 40% more revenue from personalization than slower-growing peers; this is a comparative association, not a causal estimate or a promised uplift for Lee’s Market.

Lee’s Market’s internal 2023 retail strategy document reports 45% online engagement with personalized recommendations and an associated 25% increase in average order value, but does not disclose enough methodology to establish incremental or causal lift.

A Lee’s Market Sales Strategy post reports that about 85% of transactions were linked to loyalty accounts by Q2 2024, an improvement from the previous quarter; this provides a personalization data base but does not demonstrate a sales effect.

report_insights.claim: Lee’s should test purchase-history-based offers, meal and recipe bundles, replenishment reminders, and inventory-aware substitutions across online, delivery, and store channels; grocery sources describe loyalty data, tailored incentives, and connected-channel recommendations as useful mechanisms.

Use customer-selected preferences transparently, and validate campaign value with a randomized holdout measuring incremental margin after discounts, basket value, conversion, repeat purchase, substitution acceptance, and opt-outs or complaints.
